title: Legacy CRM Recipe Apps Framework — Configurable Widget and Application Ecosystem
summary: The configurable application ecosystem for a legacy life sciences CRM, featuring recipe-based apps (full-screen experiences) and widgets (embeddable sections within existing pages) with per-device support matrices and online/offline connection modes across 15+ modules.

findings.framework_architecture: The platform uses a recipe-based configuration model where administrators compose user experiences from a catalog of pre-built apps and widgets. Apps are full-screen experiences that take over the viewport. Widgets are embeddable sections that can be placed within existing page layouts. Each module declares its supported form factors (iPad, iPhone, Web, Android Tablet, Android Phone) and connection mode (Online Only or Offline-capable with local data synchronization).
findings.account_and_territory_modules: Account Team (Widget, iPad and Web, offline-capable) displays the cross-functional team assigned to an account with role-based member visibility. Territory Status Dashboard (Widget, all five devices, online only) provides territory-level performance metrics and KPI visualization. Next Best Customer (Widget, all five devices, online only) uses algorithmic scoring to recommend which accounts to prioritize for engagement.
findings.planning_and_approval_modules: Activity Plan Completion Report (App, all five devices, online only) tracks field execution against cyclical visit plans with completion percentages and variance analysis. Plan Cycle Summary (Widget, iPad and Web, offline-capable) aggregates plan cycle performance across accounts, products, and representatives. Approval Requests (App, iPad, iPhone, and Web, online only) provides a unified queue for pending approval workflows across multiple business processes.
findings.execution_modules: Call Details History (Widget, iPad, iPhone, and Web, offline-capable) displays historical visit records with product discussions, key messages delivered, and outcomes. Call To Dos (Widget, iPad and Web, offline-capable) surfaces pending post-call action items and follow-up tasks. Quick Actions (Widget, iPad and Web, offline-capable) provides configurable shortcut buttons for frequently used operations during field visits.
findings.content_and_compliance_modules: Content Library (Widget, iPad, iPhone, and Web, offline-capable) provides access to approved marketing materials, presentations, and clinical documents with offline download capability. EPPV and MID Compliances (Widget, iPad, iPhone, and Web, offline-capable) tracks regulatory compliance requirements for educational events, post-visit payments, and medical information disclosures.
findings.engagement_and_meetings_modules: Meetings management spans multiple sub-modules: Budgets (financial allocation and tracking), Pulse (real-time event engagement metrics), Sign In Sheet (attendee capture), Speakers (speaker program management), and Topics (agenda and discussion tracking). Remote Engagements (App, iPad and Web, online only) supports video and digital detailing sessions with integrated content presentation. Sales Chart (Widget, iPad and Web, online only) visualizes sales performance trends and territory analytics.
findings.data_and_reference_modules: Reference data integration provides healthcare provider and organization data enrichment from external provider networks. Orders management handles product ordering workflows with inventory and pricing integration. Samples Management (Widget and App variants, iPad, iPhone, and Web, offline-capable) covers compliant sample distribution, signature capture, inventory reconciliation, and regulatory lot tracking.
findings.device_support_pattern: Modules follow three device support tiers: Tier 1 (all five devices — iPad, iPhone, Web, Android Tablet, Android Phone) for high-usage features like territory dashboards and activity plans. Tier 2 (iPad, iPhone, and Web) for features that require larger screen real estate or web access. Tier 3 (iPad and Web only) for features that are primarily used in office or planning contexts rather than field visits. The Android support gap in Tier 2 and Tier 3 modules reflects the platform's iOS-first heritage in life sciences field forces.
